synthesis.headline: Analysis of Nemotron-3.5-Lightning SRE Episodes Showing Strict Failure Due to Cost-Suboptimal Repairs
synthesis.interpretation: An evaluation of gradeable episodes reveals that despite achieving safe and complete recovery with high partial scores, the runs strictly fail due to non-optimal repair choices and cost deltas compared to the reference optimal action. Specifically, episode 0 failed on root cause identification and repair cost, whereas episode 1 identified the correct root cause but incurred penalties regarding initial service inventory and repair optimality. Both trials committed action R01 with a cost of 9, missing the reference optimal action R03 costing 6.
observations: Episode 0 achieved a partial score of 0.63 with a safe recovery, but failed root cause identification and used a non-optimal repair action.
Episode 1 achieved a higher partial score of 0.90385 and correctly identified the root cause, yet still strictly failed due to repair cost and inventory constraints.
Both episodes executed the committed action R01 with a cost of 9, exceeding the reference optimal cost of 6 associated with action R03.
No unsafe commits or recovery failures were recorded across the evaluated gradeable episodes.
synthesis.limitations: The findings are derived from a very small sample size of only two gradeable episodes using a single model configuration. Topology, metrics, costs, and counterfactual repairs are synthetic reconstructions rather than direct production measurements, requiring broader validation.
